_meta.description: Fast-boat crossings to the Nusa Islands. Referenced by the `ferry` field on spots in bali-spots.json.
_meta.scope: Information and outbound booking links only. The MVP processes no payments and holds no bookings.

provenance.status: UNVERIFIED — schedules and prices change constantly
provenance.note: Departure times below are indicative patterns, not a live timetable. Crossings are regularly cancelled for weather, especially December–February. The UI must present these as approximate and always defer to the operator's own site.

routes.label: Bali → Nusa Penida

departurePorts.name: Sanur Beach Port
departurePorts.note: Main departure point. Purpose-built terminal, most frequent sailings.
departurePorts.arrivesAt: Banjar Nyuh / Toya Pakeh, Nusa Penida

departurePorts.name: Padangbai Harbour
departurePorts.note: Better if you are already in East Bali. Fewer daily sailings.

indicativeSchedule.note: Last return is early. Missing it means an unplanned night on the island.

indicativePrice.note: One way per person; return tickets usually cheaper than two singles

tips: Book the earliest outbound you can stand — the island needs a full day minimum.
Boarding is a wade through shallow surf at Sanur. Your luggage will get wet.
Crossings are cancelled for swell with little notice, most often in wet season.
Arrange island transport before you sail; supply at the pier is limited and priced accordingly.

routes.label: Bali → Nusa Lembongan

departurePorts.name: Sanur Beach Port
departurePorts.note: The standard departure point for Lembongan.
departurePorts.arrivesAt: Jungutbatu or Mushroom Bay, Nusa Lembongan

indicativeSchedule.note: Fewer sailings than the Penida route; check the day before.

tips: Lembongan connects to Nusa Ceningan by a yellow suspension bridge — walk or scooter across.
Local boats run Lembongan → Penida if you want both islands in one trip.
The island is small enough to cover in a day, but it rewards an overnight.
